title: Gabber equivariant very-tame modification
statement:
Let $C$ be an integral excellent separated Noetherian scheme and $B\subset C$ a nowhere dense closed subset such that $(C,B)$ is a log regular pair. Let a finite group $G$ of order invertible on $C$ act on the pair, generically freely. Put $T=C\setminus U$, where $U$ is the largest invariant open on which $G$ acts freely. There exist an integral Noetherian scheme $C_1$ with an action of $G$, a $G$-equivariant projective morphism $f:C_1\to C$ and a dense open $C^0\subseteq C$ such that $f$ restricts to an isomorphism $f^{-1}(C^0)\to C^0$, and such that, with $B_1=f^{-1}(B\cup T)$, the pair $(C_1,B_1)$ is log regular and the action of $G$ on it is very tame. Moreover $f^{-1}(V)$ is dense in $C_1$ for any dense open $V\subset C$. Separated means that the diagonal into the product over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is a closed immersion.

Here admissible means that each orbit is contained in an affine open; generically free means free on geometric points over a dense invariant open. An action on a pair preserves its closed subset and hence its divisorial log structure. Projective here means that for every affine open $W\subseteq C$ the restriction $f^{-1}(W)\to W$ is projective in the sense of [def-kun-projective]: a closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^N_W$ followed by the projection. The log regular pair and its geometric stalks are those of [def-trf-log-regular-pair].

At a geometric point $\bar c$ of $C_1$, write $A=\mathcal O_{C_1,\bar c}$, $M$ for the divisorial log stalk, $\overline M=M/A^\times$, $I$ for the ideal generated by nonunit log sections, and $H$ for the stabilizer of the geometric point. Very tame means that $|H|$ is prime to the residue characteristic, $H$ acts trivially on $\overline M$, and $H$ acts trivially on $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. In residue characteristic zero the prime-to-characteristic condition is void.

source.place: Expose VIII Theorem 1.1, printed p.85, and IX Theorem 2.3, printed p.134; integral case of the modification construction (normalized blowup towers, VIII sections 4–5). Very tame is VI 3.1, pp.73–74.

proof.text: Equip $C$ with the divisorial fs log structure $M$ of [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. Its log triviality locus is exactly $C\setminus B$. Excellence implies quasi-excellence by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. A geometric stabilizer is a subgroup of $G$, so its order divides $|G|$; a divisor of a unit integer is a unit in every residue field. Thus the action is tame. The action preserves $B$, so it preserves $M$: pulling back a regular function invertible off $B$ again gives such a function. The assumed generic freeness is unchanged. These verify all the hypotheses of the absolute logarithmic modification theorem.

source.place: VI 1.2--1.4 and 3.1; VIII Theorem 1.1, p.85, hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-gabber-absolute-equivariant-modification] to $(C,M,G)$, with its $Z=B$ and $F=T$. Obtain a $G$-equivariant morphism $f:C_1\to C$ projective in the projective-bundle sense, with integral fs log regular source, log boundary $B_1=f^{-1}(B\cup T)$ and very tame action. The cited statement gives an isomorphism over $C\setminus(B\cup T)$, including the full inverse image. Put $C^0=C\setminus(B\cup T)$. The complement of $T$ contains a dense invariant free open by hypothesis, and the complement of $B$ is dense. Since $C$ is integral, hence irreducible [def-pc-integral-scheme], their intersection $C^0$ is dense and nonempty. The theorem [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure] identifies the source's fs log structure with the divisorial structure of $C_1\setminus B_1$. Thus its log regularity and the very tame conditions are precisely those of the pair in the item, for the stated boundary $B_1$.

source.place: VIII Theorem 1.1, sections 4--5 and Theorem 5.6.1; VI 1.4 (divisorial log structure of a log regular scheme).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper], $f$ is proper. By [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], it is in particular quasi-compact. Choose a finite affine cover of the Noetherian scheme $C$. Each inverse image is quasi-compact, so their finite union $C_1$ is quasi-compact: an open cover restricts to a finite subcover on each of these finitely many preimages. The fs log regular source is locally Noetherian by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Hence $C_1$ is Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact).

source.place: Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper); Tags 01W1 (definition-proper) and 01T1 (definition-finite-type); fs log regularity as in ILO VI 1.2.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $W\subseteq C$. The projective-bundle factorization of $f$ is a closed immersion into $\mathbf P_C(\mathcal E)$ for a finite-type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal E$ [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Restrict it to $W$. The closed immersion remains closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The affine restriction data in [def-nagata-relative-proj] identify the ambient inverse image with $\operatorname{Proj}(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)(W))$. Clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] identifies this algebra with $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_C(W)}(\mathcal E(W))$, degree by degree since both maps send degree-one sections to the same generators. Applying these same affine descriptions to $\mathcal E|_W$ identifies the ambient scheme with $\mathbf P_W(\mathcal E|_W)$. Restriction preserves the local finite generation and local module presentations defining finite type and quasi-coherence. Thus $f^{-1}(W)\to W$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense.

source.place: Tag 01W8 (definition-projective); projective-bundle restriction from its relative Proj affine charts; Tag 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion).

proof.text: The structure sheaf $\mathcal O_W$ is ample: in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], take $n=1$ and $s=1$, so $W_s=W$ is affine; $W$ is quasi-compact as an affine open of the Noetherian scheme $C$. Apply [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] to the restricted morphism from the previous step. It is H-projective, meaning exactly a closed immersion $f^{-1}(W)\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_W$ followed by projection [def-kun-projective]. This proves the required projectivity for each affine open $W$; $W$ need not be invariant under $G$.

Let $V\subseteq C$ be any dense open. Since $C$ is integral, $V\cap C^0$ is a nonempty open. By the full-preimage isomorphism over $C^0$, its inverse image is a nonempty open of $C_1$. Integrality of $C_1$ makes every nonempty open dense [def-pc-integral-scheme]. This dense open lies in $f^{-1}(V)$, so $f^{-1}(V)$ is dense. This also covers $V=C$, dimension zero, and the trivial group; no positive-dimensional hypothesis was used.

It adds no new nodes, and the item statement is byte-identical to the one I repaired in Q70. Source: ILO VIII Thm 1.1 (printed p.85, pdf p.90), which asks for X noetherian, qe, separated and fs log regular, G tame and generically free, Z the non-triviality locus and T the non-free locus; it gives a projective modification with Z'=f^-1(Z∪T) and a very tame action. The split cites the existing unsplit lem-per-gabber-absolute-equivariant-modification (Q18), which is more general (fs log regular, quasi-excellent input, plus the four-stage tower). Step 1 checks every hypothesis of that node: the divisorial M is fs with triviality locus C∖B, excellent implies quasi-excellent, stabilizer orders divide |G| so the action is tame, preserving B means acting by log automorphisms, and its Z,F are this item's B,T. Step 2: the absolute node gives an integral, fs log regular, very tame source and an isomorphism over C∖(B∪T), meaning the full preimage. C^0 is dense because two nonempty opens of an irreducible scheme meet. lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure says the source structure equals O∩j_*O_V^× with V dense, so (C1,B1) is a log regular pair, and the very-tame conditions match word for word. Step 3: 01WC properness gives quasi-compactness, and def-trf-fs-log-blowup works over locally Noetherian schemes, so C1 is Noetherian. Step 4 (elementary): the projective bundle restricts to an affine W through i_W and Sym clause (b). Step 5: O_W is ample with n=1, s=1, so 087S(1) makes f^-1(W)→W H-projective. Step 6: a nonempty preimage in an integral C1 is dense. Small and edge cases checked: ILO 1.2(a) (A², ±1, blowup of 0), trivial G, empty boundary, dimension 0, empty W. There is no cycle, and no SGA source is cited. I accept the five off-unit tool_uses. Batch-5 flags: I walked the closure of each flagged node (stmt_deps and proof_deps, stopping at nt-assume) and none contains thm-trf, sk-thm, a trace node or a sec-poincare-duality node. log-regular-divisorial-structure is general monoid and toric algebra (Nizioł, VI 1.4), projective-bundle-proper is 01WC, fs-log-blowup and projective-bundle-morphism are definitions, and projective-bundle-to-h-projective is 087S. All are general scheme theory or log geometry, outside both assumptions, so I accept them. Maintainer note: the item and the absolute node overlap (both state VIII 1.1, both created 2026-10-19 by different groups). That overlap is in the base, not this delivery, and reusing the general node is the correct response.
